summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics) with the harness assurance_generated_test.go; scratch removed. This turn closes a limitation I recorded twice on the ReadIndex findings by exercising the deferred-read path, and records its mechanism as sourced knowledge. New child question @queued_read_index_release (parent 708eebc14c4040feb495e11d064001d0-question-0) plus a Behavior entry for the mechanism: stepLeader defers a MsgReadIndex into r.pendingReadIndexMessages with no heartbeat while the leader has no committed entry in its term (raft.go:1346-1363), and releasePendingReadIndexMessages runs only from the MsgAppResp commit path (raft.go:1542-1546, 2123-2157). The experiment makes a real node win an election without follower acknowledgment, submits a local ReadIndex (recording queue size, heartbeats emitted and delivered read states), then delivers the replication messages and the followers' acknowledgments to drive the first commit, and submits a second ReadIndex afterwards as the contrast path. The single comparison encodes the duty that a deferred request is released by the commit that makes the read index available; it is expected to hold, which is recorded as a sourced negative/confirmatory result rather than forced into a violation. Construction-time local runs show, for the record and not as formal evidence, that the queued request is held with zero heartbeats while committed_in_term is false, is released once the follower acknowledgments make the term's first commit (queue back to 0, one read state with index 1, nothing undelivered), and that a later request is served through the usual ReadOnlySafe path with two voter acknowledgments. The formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained receipt.
